findings.location: ## Definition, “The least denominator is the denominator in lowest terms”: sentence stating that the integer quotient agrees with real division and citing lem-of-naturals-positive

The surrounding embedding dependencies may support an elementary derivation, but this citation does not establish the quoted quotient claim. Derive it from the field embeddings and division, or cite a result that states it.

findings.location: ## Definition, “The least denominator is the denominator in lowest terms”: sentence “Since d divides q(x), q(x)/d is a natural number ≥ 1”
findings.evidence: Divisibility supplies an integer quotient k with q(x)=d k. The text does not show that k is positive or identify it with a natural number. Write q(x)=d k, use q(x)>0 and d>0 to obtain k≥1 in the integer order, then use the natural embedding; alternatively cite an exact quotient-positivity result.

findings.location: ## Definition, “The class is strictly larger than the continuous functions”: the claim that the indicator of a single point is Baire class one
findings.evidence: The item asserts this witness property without giving an approximating sequence or citing one. For a∈[0,1], the continuous tent functions φ_n(x)=max(0,1−n|x−a|) converge pointwise to the indicator of {a}; add this construction and the direct discontinuity check.

L3 supplies a natural m≥1, but the item’s dependencies do not establish that every nonzero natural is a successor. The published lemma lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor states the needed fact; add it to deps and cite it, or prove the predecessor step.
